PROMPT

Build "Lock Jelly." — a single self-contained HTML file (WebGPU + WGSL, no libraries, no network, works from file://), part of a "Material Studies" series of jelly dioramas. If WebGPU is missing or the adapter fails, show a clean fallback card instead of the scene.

CONCEPT
A square block of clear coloured jelly (about 5.2 × 5.2 units, ~2 units high) holding a little English canal scene. The canal runs along the FRONT edge of the block, so the block's front face cuts the water lengthways: you see the lock chamber in cross-section, the water inside it rising and falling between the gates, fish swimming, the boat's hull below the waterline. All cut faces show candy-coloured soil strata; under the pounds a blue-grey puddle-clay lining, under the chamber a brick invert on a concrete bed, under the fields brown earth and turf.

LAYOUT (left to right along the front)
- Upper pound on the left at the higher level, opening into a round winding hole (a bay for turning boats); near the lock it narrows between brick wing walls.
- The lock chamber in the middle: brick walls with dressed-stone quoins and coping, a slimy band between the two water levels and weed below, an iron ladder, a gauge board, a stone cill under the top gate, recesses that the open gates fold into.
- Below the bottom gate a short walled tail, then the lower pound bends away from the front face, runs under a humpback brick bridge into a basin with a willow-covered island, lily pads in its corners and a sunken bicycle on the bed.
- The ground steps down from an upper terrace to a lower one along a grassy bank.
- Behind the lock: stone setts around the chamber, bollards, a gravel towpath, a lane, the keeper's whitewashed cottage with a slate roof, green door, picket-fence garden full of flowers and washing flapping on a line, a gas lamp, a bench, a white windmill with turning lattice sails, oaks, willows, poplars, a hedge, sheep, reeds on the soft banks.

WATER
- Linear shallow-water waves on a staggered grid (~168²) with a little surface tension, so short ripples are springy like jelly; damping and firmness are adjustable.
- Three separate bodies of water — upper pound, chamber, lower pound — each with its own rest level. Faces between bodies stay shut unless the gate between them is open and the levels are equal. The chamber's level is moved bodily when paddles are drawn (Torricelli-style flow), with boils, white water and a dimple at the intake.
- Rendering: refraction of the scene behind, flavour-coloured absorption, sun caustics on the bed, soft light shafts, foam (wakes, paddle churn), a meniscus line on the cut faces. Split the surface mesh along the gate lines so the step in level at a shut gate is a clean wall hidden by the gate leaf, not a ramp.
- The block itself can be tipped by dragging its side; the jelly shears and wobbles, the water sloshes, and it settles back.

THE LOCK AND THE KEEPER
- Two single-leaf timber gates (planks, rails, diagonal brace, iron straps, a walkway with a handrail), each with a white balance beam with black bands. Ground-paddle pedestals with toothed racks that rise when wound.
- An articulated lock keeper (flat cap, navy jumper, cords, windlass in hand; torso, arms, thighs and shins as separate parts). He walks with a proper gait, plans his route around the bench, pedestals, bollards and any beam lying across his way (going round the beam's end), leans his back on a beam and walks it round backwards to swing a gate, winds the windlass with his arm circling the spindle, and sits on his bench between jobs. He sets off for the gate as the boat comes in.
- The cycle: the boat lies in the full chamber → keeper shuts the top gate → winds up the bottom paddles → the chamber empties into the tail with white water → winds them down → opens the bottom gate → the boat leaves, runs the tail, swings round the bend, ducks under the bridge, goes round the island and comes back into the chamber bow first → shut bottom gate → round to the top paddles → chamber fills with boils → open the top gate → the boat goes up the pound, turns in the winding hole and comes back. Repeat forever. A gate may only open when the levels match.

BOATS
- A traditional narrowboat "Wobble": black lofted hull, a green cabin with red lining-out, brass portholes, a cratch board and cover at the bow, a chimney with brass bands (puffing smoke), a painted Buckby can, plank and pole on the roof, rope fenders, a headlamp, a brass swan-neck tiller and a steerer in a red jumper. It follows smooth filleted routes (check the stern never swings out through the block's face), slows near the gates, heaves, pitches and rolls on the local surface, and hands its displaced volume back to the water so it makes bow waves and wakes.
- Three moored narrowboats in the basin in different liveries with flowerpots on the roofs and one ginger cat, tied to bank pins with stretchy mooring lines.

LIFE
- Roach, perch and bream as boids that stay in their own body of water (they can only move between pound and chamber while a gate is open), under the surface and hulls, off the bed, scattering from the boat and splashes.
- Mallards (drakes, ducks) and a duck with four ducklings that follow exactly along her trail; a pair of mute swans in the basin. They paddle the surface, ride the chamber down and up, upend now and then, get out of the boat's way and come for bread.
- A grey heron that wades in the shallows or stands on a moored boat's roof, stabs at fish (sometimes catching one), and flaps off somewhere quieter when the boat passes or someone toots.
- Chimney smoke from the boat and the cottage.

UI (editorial, like a print magazine)
- Top-left: small caps eyebrow "MATERIAL STUDIES", a huge italic serif title "Lock / Jelly.", a short subtitle. Top-right: a status pill "WebGPU · Live / Paused / Unavailable".
- Right: a frosted-glass control panel (a bottom sheet on mobile) with: buttons Hurry (speeds the keeper, paddles and boat), Toot (horn; also Space), Throw bread, Rubber duck (drops a yellow rubber duck that floats upright, can be picked up and thrown, rides the lock, is stopped by gates and shoved by boats); a liveliness meter; tallies Trips · Lockfuls · Fed; a status line "Wobble — Emptying the lock 62%" telling the story step by step; three flavours Greengage, Elderflower, Blackcurrant (change the water colour/absorption and strata); sliders Firmness, Wave damping, Paddle speed; Reset, Pause, Sound on/off, View.
- Bottom-left: "How to play — Throw bread. Toot the horn. Hurry the keeper." with a small line of instructions.
- Interaction: drag across the water to make waves, drag the block's side to tip it, pick up and throw rubber ducks, drag empty space to orbit, scroll/pinch to zoom; touch works.
- Soft studio lighting on a warm paper backdrop with the block's tinted, caustic-flecked shadow; WebAudio sounds: the boat's horn, the gate thudding shut, a creak, the windlass ratchet, and the rush of water that swells with the flow.

QUALITY
Keep it smooth (fixed-step physics, cheap per frame), no console errors, no page scroll, works at phone width. Test it headlessly: a full round trip happens, levels go exactly from upper to lower and back, no gate opens across a step, the keeper never walks into the water or through obstacles, the boat never touches a gate leaf, and every button works.
x-2110014604524896392:
PROMPT

Build a single-file interactive WebGL diorama (one index.html, no build step) with Three.js r160 loaded via an import map from http://cdn.jsdelivr.net, plus OrbitControls and BufferGeometryUtils (mergeVertices, mergeGeometries) from three/examples/jsm. Everything is procedural — no external models or textures.

CONCEPT
"Torii at High Tide": a miniature Japanese shrine island inspired by Itsukushima, inside a 10×10 block of clear water with rounded edges (vertical corner radius ~0.6, top edge radius ~0.26), on a thin sand-colored base slab, on a warm washi-paper background with a soft floor shadow that fades out with distance (so long dusk shadows never streak across the page).

TERRAIN (heightfield ~400×400, clipped to the rounded block, with a boundary "skirt" so the cross-section shows through the water)
- Work in a local frame facing the camera (u = across, v = toward the viewer).
- A forested dome-shaped hill at the back (~2.4 high), a low sandy shrine terrace at its foot, then a wide, gently sloping tidal flat in front (from ~-0.06 down to ~-0.46), dropping to ~-1.0 at the front and sides.
- Two rocky granite headlands framing the bay, each with 1–2 leaning bonsai-style pines (segmented trunks + flattened canopy pads).
- A flattened clearing on the hill flank for the pagoda.
- Terrain shader: granite rock on steep slopes (speckled, darker wet band just above the waterline, algae-dark below it), sand with a wet line, darker wet intertidal sand below the high-tide mark, moss/grass on the hill and in patches on the terrace, snow on upward-facing surfaces in winter, procedural animated caustics under water. CPU-baked horizon AO per vertex plus canopy-cover darkening.

ARCHITECTURE (merge everything into one vertex-colored mesh + one emissive "glow" mesh; write a small Builder that adds boxes/cylinders/spheres/custom geometry with a color and a transform, then mergeGeometries)
- Ryōbu-style torii standing in the bay on the axis of the shrine (~1.9 tall): vermilion tapered main pillars with black base sheaths, four supporting sode-bashira legs with black caps and two connecting beams each, nuki tie beam, central strut with a dark plaque, shimaki, and a curved kasagi (extruded shape with upturned ends) with a black top layer. Pillars must end inside the shimaki, not poke through the kasagi.
- Shrine on stilts over the tidal flat: plank deck (with plank-gap strips and dark edge beams) on a grid of wooden stilts reaching the seabed; a main hall and a smaller front hall (white walls, vermilion posts and tie beams, shoji-style front panels = glow panels behind a thin dark lattice), a lower front stage with vermilion railings, and two roofed vermilion corridors on stilts running sideways then back to the shore.
- Roofs: a hip-roof generator with a concave profile and lifted eave corners (top surface dark cypress-bark brown, warm wood underside, pale fascia trim, black ridge cap).
- A five-storey pagoda on the hill clearing: stone plinth, white walls with vermilion posts, bracket layer, flared roofs decreasing in size, bronze finial with rings.
- Stone tōrō lanterns on the terrace and on the stage (hexagonal base, post, firebox with emissive windows, small roof, jewel).

VEGETATION
- ~4–5k canopy blobs (InstancedMesh of icospheres with vertex-noise displacement + fragment bump), clustered 2–4 per tree, per-instance AO from neighbour occlusion, brighter tops.
- Four kinds via an instance attribute: broadleaf, cherry, maple, pine (flattened pads). Cherries cluster lower on the hill and as 5 feature trees with visible trunks on the terrace; pines dominate the summit and the headlands.
- Colors come from per-kind dark/light palette uniforms that the JS blends across seasons.

SEASONS (cyclic 0..4 = spring, summer, autumn, winter; animated transition from a dock button)
- Spring: pink sakura, falling petals. Summer: lush green, no particles. Autumn: red maples, orange/yellow broadleaf, falling maple leaves. Winter: bare-ish brown deciduous blobs shrunk ~38%, snow on canopy tops, roofs, decks, rocks and ground; snowfall that melts instantly on the water.

WATER (realistic, not jelly)
- Pipeline: opaque scene → MSAA HalfFloat target with DepthTexture; copy to a second target, then draw the water with a custom ShaderMaterial doing a manual depth test; then floating particles; final fullscreen pass with ACES tone mapping, sRGB, subtle tilt-shift. Transparent canvas over the CSS background.
- Color from real thickness: reconstruct the depth behind each water pixel, Beer–Lambert absorption toward a deep scatter color derived from the user's water color (pale over the flats, blue in the deep; side walls get extra path length so they read as a water volume).
- Screen-space refraction, Fresnel sky reflection, sun glints from fine animated detail normals.
- Screen-space reflections (~26 ray-march steps against the depth buffer, fewer on mobile) so the torii, shrine and lit lanterns reflect in the water.
- Ripples: GPU wave equation on a 256×256 HalfFloat ping-pong target, fixed 60 Hz steps, land-mask texture so waves reflect off the shore. Cursor movement injects capsule drops along its path; a click makes a splash.
- Shore foam only where the terrain is near the water level AND gently sloped (no white outlines around cliffs, stilts or the torii pillars); foam band width scaled by slope; broken by noise.
- Tide: a dock toggle animates between high tide (0) and low tide (-0.55): the water block's rim moves and its sides stretch; at low tide the whole flat is exposed and the torii stands on wet sand.

PARTICLES (petals / leaves / snow, ~700 instanced quads, CPU-simulated)
- Spawn from cherry blobs (spring), deciduous blobs (autumn) or the sky (winter); flutter while falling; a gusting wind blows from the island toward the bay so they reach the water.
- Landing: on water they become floating (vertex shader lifts them by the same ripple + wave height as the water), drift slowly, get pushed by the cursor's movement and blown away by click splashes, strand when the tide drops, re-float when it rises; on land they rest and fade.
- Shapes drawn in the fragment shader: notched petal, five-lobed maple leaf, soft snow disc. Manual depth test against the scene depth.

KOI
- 7 koi (lathe body + forked fan tail + pectoral fins, merged), InstancedMesh with a swimming sway in the vertex shader and procedural patterns per type (kohaku, sanke, showa, ogon, plain orange). They wander, steer away from shallow water and the block walls, and flee the cursor and splashes. Rendered under the water so they are refracted and tinted.

TIME OF DAY (slider, shown as a clock from 11:00 to ~19:10)
- Sun elevation, color and intensity, hemisphere colors, and the water's sky reflection shift from noon to golden hour; towards dusk the shoji panels and lanterns glow (emissive) and three warm point lights light the shrine, the stage and the torii.

UI (editorial, minimal, English)
Brand "shiosai°" with a small torii mark, headline "A gate that / stands in the sea.", eyebrow "Shrine and tide, in miniature", a vertical caption "A study of tide and seasons", a location label "Shrine Cove · 34°16′ N · 132°19′ E", a floating pill dock (reset, season cycle with the current season name, High tide / Low tide toggle, Tune, fullscreen), hints and an adaptive FPS + "Season · time" readout in the footer, a glassy settings panel (season, time of day, falling petals; water color, tide level, wave height, ripple strength, clarity, caustics; sun azimuth, tilt-shift), and a "How it's made" card. Vermilion accent, light and dark themes via CSS tokens, responsive to 390 px (panel becomes a bottom sheet), prefers-reduced-motion respected, adaptive pixel ratio and a lighter mode for touch devices. Intro: the water fills the block while the camera eases in.
